name: WooCommerce
oneLiner: Free, open-source ecommerce plugin for WordPress with no plan fees or revenue share. You pay separately for hosting, paid extensions and card processing.
summary: WooCommerce is a free, open-source plugin that turns a self-hosted WordPress site into an online store, with no subscription tiers and no cut of sales. The bill comes from elsewhere: hosting (Woo estimates $25–$350/month for most stores), paid extensions at $29–$299 a year each, and card processing, which through Woo's own WooPayments costs 2.9% + $0.30 per US card charge. You own the code and can change host or payment gateway without penalty, but updates, backups and plugin compatibility are your job.
notFor: Owners who want hosting, security and updates handled by one vendor on one bill
Stores with nobody to maintain WordPress, plugin updates and backups, in-house or through an agency
pros: Core plugin is free and open source, with 0% revenue share and no plan tiers
No extra fee for using a third-party payment gateway, and you can run several gateways at once
WooPayments has no setup or monthly fee: 2.9% + $0.30 per US card transaction
Unlimited products, orders and product variants on the free core
Paid extensions keep working if you stop renewing; you lose only updates and support
You pick and can switch your host, from $25/month on Woo-recommended Pressable
cons: Hosting is not included and is billed separately by a third-party host
Key features are paid yearly per-site extensions: Subscriptions $279/year, Bookings $249/year
Extension renewals charge the list price at renewal time, and coupons don't apply
WooPayments adds 1.5% for international cards, 1% for currency conversion and $15 per dispute
Support for the free core plugin is only through the WordPress.org community forums
Costs are spread across host, extensions and payments, so there is no single all-in price
